reviews.title: Outstanding case for the price range
reviews.comment: This was my first dual-chamber case, and I will not go back to the older style.  The 380 TG was very easy to build in.  There was plenty of room to run cables.  Mounting 3 additional fans and a 360mm liquid cooler was a breeze, with plenty of room to run everything inside the case's main chamber.  I also appreciated the motherboard being slightly raised, with grommets running along the 24-pin side.  This allows for the versatility of where to run the cables and wires, exactly where you need them, while maintaining a clean look.  The glass panels look great, and I appreciate that they took the time to put protective film on the inside of the case as well.  The case seems well-built, but only time will tell if that holds true. My only issue with the case is that the brackets covering the GPU ports are not screwed in, so they have to be broken off to slot your GPU into the motherboard.  It may be nitpicky for a $70 case, but I don't like the idea of being forced to permanently remove something from it.
reviews.author: Dack Man

reviews.title: A Nice PC Case
reviews.comment: If you want a mid-size PC case has a lot of room for cable management and to display RGB lighting this is a good case.  It has plenty of room for your components, a lot of room behind the MOBO for cable routing and room for two SSD drives and more.  With 3 fans it is whisper quiet while providing plenty of airflow.  I only added one extra fan in the top of the case.  All panels are very easy to remove requiring from 0 to 2 screws at most.  I only have two (Minor) complaints, one is no bays for a CDROM/DVR drive, but I solved that by buying an external USB drive.  The other is the slot covers you remove to access the add-in cards (GPU) are not screwed in, once removed always removed unless glued or taped back in place.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Plenty of room, looks great.
reviews.comment: This is a sweet little aquarium, with enough lights that you don't need or probably want any more inside. It is setup to hide the PSU and all the wiring and it is still smaller then the last case i replaced with this one. I also holds the 360 radiator on top with the fans installed and is still above the mobo enough to move the fan plugins if you need to. I think they could have made more hard drive mounting spots as there is plenty of room but I just stacked my six in the bottom in the back with room to spare. It come fully assembled and the fans are quiet enough to run at full speed without any noise and with an AIO cooler my I9 idles in the low 20's.Honestly it is so uncluttered it looks like it should have a lizard lying around in there, yeah for it's price it is really nice.
reviews.author: shadowdr

reviews.title: Great PC Case to Build, Many Features
reviews.comment: I usually never write reviews, but I was blown away by the design and overall finished product that I felt inclined to share my experience. This is a very versatile PC case IMHO, great for both those stepping into the world of PC Building and Seasoned PC Builders alike.  Initially the look alone is what lead me to give this TT View 380 a try as I was wanting to upgrade my case for a cleaner overall look, but I received much more.  This case is well worth the price ($99.00 at time of this review), no doubt about it.  It features support for the forthcoming BTF Hidden connector design for those who want to be ready for the direction that Motherboard manufacturers are headed in, as well as Hideaway PSU mounting support behind motherboard, interior rubber grommet access for feeding 24v MOBO connector, SATA and other MOBO cables. I went with a top mounted radiator configuration.  The SSD/HDD tray allows for support of 1 HDD and 2 SSD easy mounting with enough room for cable storage behind.  The 4 pre-installed fans is great, add those with the 2 fans for my radiator and I am starting with 6 fans all synced beautifully together with support for 3 more on the bottom due to the decision to move mounting of the PSU behind the motherboard. If I had to find a con, it would be the pop out PCI-E port brackets. I personally would prefer these to be removable and able to be removed/replaced based on ones need.  Also, I do have a rattling noise from my radiator fans that I am still trying to figure out if it is my AIO or an issue with the mount support, as I did not have this issue in the case I just moved from.  Still testing and will update once I figure out what is really going on. Overall: Awesome Case, Beautiful Case for a Great Price Based on all the features.  This has definitely opened eyes and I even have friends ordering this exact case. Great Job Thermaltake!!!!
reviews.author: Chill Will

reviews.title: Awesome case. 10/10 would recommend
reviews.comment: It’s a perfect fit with my ASUS B650E-E WiFi motherboard, gigabyte nvidia 5070 gpu, thermalright liquid cooler and my 850w century 2 psu. Everything fit perfectly. I never had to move any screws around. I currently have 7 fans in the case and have room for 3 more if I want for maximum cooling; there are even slots at the top of the motherboard area so wires to go through it made everything clean with easy cable management and a super easy build.
reviews.author: Alex Burch
